pr_title: Improve stream playback on high latency cameras
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Input cameras with high latencies can cause playback issues when using stream. This PR:
1) Copies the global stream settings into each stream, so they can be modified on a per stream basis by setting stream_options. They can also be modified by the stream worker.
2) Adds the option to increase the timeout when waiting for the stream worker to get the next part and uses this timeout in the Nest integration.
3) Disables ll-hls when an hls input is detected. This should fix issues with Netatmo cameras.

./segment/32.m4s

#EXT-X-PART:DURATION=0.867,URI="./segment/34.1.m4s"
#EXT-X-PART:DURATION=0.933,URI="./segment/34.2.m4s"

I've seen this happen a couple times now with a similar pattern where in the of the segment it fails, then the segment is missing.

Did having the additional 3 seconds of timeout reduce the number of 404s vs before?
What I think is happening in your playlists above is that the stream from Nest is breaking in segment 33, and so the segment doesn't complete. Since the worker is restarted, a discontinuity gets flagged, and `HlsStreamOutput.discontinuity()` will remove segment 33 since it is not complete. When the new input stream's packets come in, those are muxed into segment 34, but `#EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY` is not set yet because we only put it in above the segment and not above the parts: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/b9e93207e39cf23d7a14a23bdef4777ee77dc493/homeassistant/components/stream/core.py#L137
I think the RFC is a bit unclear on what to do in this case - I don't think the playlists are supposed to be changed, meaning the parts of segment 33 probably shouldn't be removed like that, but at the same time we don't have a full segment there so we can't just leave those parts in.
We could try moving the `#EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY` tag up above the parts to see if that improves things - I think it makes more sense up there anyhow.

I didn't see a lot of requests with between 2-3 second delays, but it may have just been circumstances of the network conditions. Hard to say without running in "production", so happy to check this in and watch it over a longer time period.  It makes sense as a change to me.

Do you see anything in the playlist indicating a discontinuity? That makes sense, but I didn't see the sequence numbers bump.

I don't see anything there indicating a discontinuity besides the missing parts. But with the current code, the discontinuity won't be flagged until the next segment is ready - the sequence number at the beginning reflects the sequence number of the first segment which is still the old one, and the discontinuity tag won't hit until the next segment is finished. You can confirm it by seeing what happens just after that - or does the player just give up and stop sending requests at that point?
I'm not sure moving just moving the discontinuity tag up will help anything, but we can try that first. If that doesn't work perhaps we can try to also salvage the leftover parts of the previous stream.
Thanks, i'll keep an eye out, i didn't think to look in the error logs and can do that next time.

issue_context.title: Generic Camera m3u8 stream request timeout causes buffering during playback
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have a Netatmo outdoor camera in my Wi-Fi that exposes its video stream via a `.m3u8` stream. In playback, Home Assistant queries the next parts to play, but some requests result in a 404 NOT FOUND. This is not a problem by itself, but the request has a timeout of apparently 2 seconds:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9069888/169041112-a3721665-9191-4cd4-b26b-78babf2d711c.png)

These 2 seconds cause a delay in loading the next chunks, ultimately causing the playback to buffer for ~500-1000ms every few seconds.

I have no idea why some of these `playlist.m3u8` calls fail, as other calls work. I have no idea how m3u8 streams work, but I assume this is by design, as the `HLS_msn` increases by one, as soon as the previous request fails.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9069888/169042311-8a8a0866-95ff-41f8-8d10-db114c312c8e.png)


Most responses ( `.m4s`) are <1000ms, so in my case setting the timeout from 2000ms to 1000ms would probably solve this issue. These are the requests sorted by Time:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9069888/169042592-01fa5060-4877-433f-86ff-2cfa4d2a23c2.png)

Should the timeout maybe be configurable?

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.5.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Generic Camera

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/generic

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9069888/169040806-6a370d64-3b74-4cbd-9d27-183a0d70f4d3.png)

The stream works flawlessly when called from JS, using [`hls.js`](https://github.com/video-dev/hls.js/). This is the code I use

```html
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/hls.js@latest"></script>
  <script>
    const streams = [
      'http://<internal_ip>/<id>/live/index.m3u8', // camera 1
      'http://<internal_ip>/<id>/live/index.m3u8', // camera 2
    ]

    streams.forEach(stream => {
      const video = document.createElement('video')
      video.autoplay = true
      video.muted = true
      container.appendChild(video)
      const hls = new Hls()
      hls.loadSource(stream)
      hls.attachMedia(video)
    })
  </script>
```
comments:
Hey there @davet2001, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`generic`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L370) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Using the same URLs that Home Assistant is using, but using hls.js, I get the same behavior, where the requests time out and cause the playback to buffer/stutter.
@hunterjm @uvjustin Do you have any ideas about this?  I don't have enough detailed knowledge about what is going on underneath to give good suggestions on this.

I think it's what I mentioned [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/issues/11018#issuecomment-1000596496). The netatmo camera feed is itself hls, which comes in segments. The player is basing its time off of the latency to HA, but that causes it to sometimes get ahead of the slower netatmo hls feed.
I guess there are a few approaches we can take for these:
1) Instead of remuxing the feed we can just proxy it
2) We could pass the feed directly to the frontend, similar to what we do with WebRTC
3) We could have core detect the hls feed and tell the frontend not to adjust the playback speed
4) We could have a frontend toggle to not adjust the playback speed

I like the idea of sending the HLS url to the player directly. e.g. instead of what `_async_stream_endpoint_url` ([link](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/edd7a3427ca0522b907df91c9bd9cae40bbb9f33/homeassistant/components/camera/__init__.py#L988) does today by returning a link to the stream component, return the camera url directly -- however, this has implications in that it wouldn't be available remotely. (I'm not sure how common hls cameras are to indicate it's work proxying, but assuming its not common)

FWIW I've seen this type of 404s or nest cloud cameras also, but not consistently enough to dig into it. 

I'm not sure I totally understand yet all the playback speed implications, but returning more bits/settings in the existing websocket doesn't sound so bad.

Yeah, while proxying would make the most sense for maintaining the HA core <-> frontend architecture while disrupting the stream the least (audio would work), it would require a totally separate implementation from what we do in stream. Also, some of the benefits like recording or grabbing frames would be lost. It's a lot of work for limited benefit, and I don't think it makes sense overall.
Remuxing like we do now seems fine overall. The main issue is just that we are trying to get a low latency feed from a high latency feed which is just not achievable. The easiest solution is just to turn off LL-HLS for those specific entities, but that itself would require some changes as LL-HLS is currently a system-wide option on the backend.
Forwarding the HLS url to the player itself as you mention also seems fine, but as you mentioned the issue is remote viewing - seems like a no go if the HLS endpoint is actually the camera itself and not the cloud.

> I think it's what I mentioned [here](https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/issues/11018#issuecomment-1000596496). The netatmo camera feed is itself hls, which comes in segments. The player is basing its time off of the latency to HA, but that causes it to sometimes get ahead of the slower netatmo hls feed. I guess there are a few approaches we can take for these:

Yes, this is exactly the behavior I experienced as well. The stream buffers, and causes the playback to speed up to make up lost time, but then buffers again.

In case of netatmo cameras, the stream is exposed via http. I access Home Assistant via https however, so in order to be able to play from the camera directly, I'd need to proxy it. 

What do you mean by *the issue is remote viewing*? HA is in the same network/LAN as the cameras, so direct access should work (disregarding the http/https issue).

One of the solutions we mentioned is just forwarding the URL to the frontend device itself, effectively bypassing HA. That would work if your client is on the internal network, but generally it wouldn't work remotely.
I think trying to turn off LL-HLS is probably the best solution for us.
Can you try disabling LL-HLS and seeing if the problem is resolved? Just add this to your configuration.yaml:
```
stream:
  ll_hls: false
```
I'm guessing that will fix the buffering issue. However, I'd be interested to see the latency - specifically if there is a large difference between viewing the HA stream (i.e. the playlist.m3u8 that comes from HA) and viewing the m3u8 from the camera itself.

> One of the solutions we mentioned is just forwarding the URL to the frontend device itself, effectively bypassing HA. That would work if your client is on the internal network, but generally it wouldn't work remotely.

Could this be set via a flag in the configuration.yaml? I think in a lot of cases the camera's feed can be reached from within the internal network. 

`ll_hls: false` completely fixed the buffering issue. Also, there are no 404 requests anymore.

I will compare the latency later when I get a chance to!
@uvjustin There is about a 8-9s delay with `ll_hls: false`. I compared with the official app, which also has a 8-9s delay. Should I also test with `ll_hls: true`?

No need, that makes sense - our regular hls implementation should only have a slight delay compared to a hls input feed, so one potential solution is to just disable ll-hls for hls inputs.
That would work here but might not be as effective for other "bursty" but non hls inputs like those @allenporter has seen. We'll discuss and see if we can find a solution which works for both these classes of cameras.

review_comments: Are the changes here in core related to the bigger change? They appear like a separate cleanup.
This change was in order to move up the discontinuity tag (in response to our discussion in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/72547#issuecomment-1140632426) while still printing pretty.
